owner: W1-26 round 2 — the opening, as a played scene.
source: RI-DLG01 §A ('the player begins with exactly nine topics, granted at character creation'); ARBITRATION S35 ('wayfinding must still work without opening the map at all: signposts, spoken directions and landmarks are unaffected'); ARBITRATION §3 CONSUMPTION.
note: DO NOT REGENERATE. Every line here is hand-written. tools/dialogue/gen-*.mjs must not target this file.
why: MEASURED, over all 336 NPC records carrying a `topics` array, through the live reader (converse.js buildTopicIndex + infoFor): of the nine ROOT topics in `00-roots.json` — the nine words that ARE the verb 'ask' — SEVEN ARE LISTED BY ZERO SPEAKERS IN THE PROVINCE. duties 0, specific-place 0, someone-in-particular 0, services 0, my-trade 0, latest-rumors 0, little-secret 0. `background` is listed by 260 and answerable by 67, so 193 people advertise it and have nothing to say. `little-advice` 3.

The reason is not the list, it is the MOUTHS. Every root info in `00-roots.json` is written for one of the six archetypes in `dialogue/speakers.json` — legionary, rootkeeper, sapcutter, mudborn, archivist, magister. But the NPC records use EIGHTEEN actor names, and the twelve that are not archetypes carry 257 of the 336 people: townsman 72, villager 37, merchant 29, healer 29, dres-factor 25, clerk 20, innkeeper 19, fisher 10, town-elder 9, and four smaller. `infoFor` will not put another actor's line in a person's mouth (correctly — that is how a net-mender came to speak a Dres factor's words, and it was fixed), so those 257 people cannot answer any of the nine.

That lands on THIS piece and not on somebody else's, because ALL THREE SPEAKERS IN THE OPENING ARE AMONG THEM: `jeeh-ei` is a `villager` and `warden-scribe-tuleeh-ma` and `clerk-avelia-doren` are `clerk`s. Measured before this file existed: the nine roots against the opening's three records returned nine nulls apiece, twenty-seven of twenty-seven. So the scene that is supposed to teach the player that asking is the verb was the one scene in which asking could not be answered by a living soul.

This file writes the `villager` and `clerk` halves of all nine. It is scoped to the two actors the opening puts in front of the player rather than to all twelve, because the other ten are other pieces' voices and a builder who writes 108 lines in ten voices he does not own is regenerating somebody else's file with extra steps. The gap that remains is named in `remaining` below rather than left to be discovered.

The lines are written for ANY villager and ANY clerk, not for Jeeh-Ei and Tuleeh-Ma. A line about a specific person belongs on that person's record (`npc.lines`), which is the tier above this one and which the opening already uses for six subjects.

EVERY info here carries `to`. That is the point of the file and not decoration: a root topic that answers and hands back nothing teaches the player that asking produces prose, which is the opposite of the lesson. 456 of the 638 infos in this tree carry `to` and it is read by `Engine.conversationSay()` into `sim.quest.topicsKnown`. Ten of thirty-five quests now open from a cold start by walking into two towns and asking what people are saying; these are the words you ask with.

PROSE REGISTER: written against `orchestration/status/W1-PROSE-TICS.json`. No `-body` indefinites (ours ran 131x Morrowind's rate before that pass; the corpus went 768 -> 2 and this file does not put them back). Contractions are used in the villager's mouth and withheld from the clerk's, because that pass's largest unfixed finding is that our NPCs use contractions at 0.06x Morrowind's rate while a clerk reading out a schedule of fees genuinely should not.

remaining.what: Ten actor names still have no root infos and therefore cannot answer any of the nine words: townsman (72 records), merchant (29), healer (29), dres-factor (25), innkeeper (19), fisher (10), town-elder (9), outlaw (2), mercenary (2), naga-elder (2), deep-elder (1).
remaining.effect: Adding villager and clerk moves the province from 79 of 336 speakers able to answer a root topic to 136 of 336. It does not reach 336, and this file does not claim to.
remaining.who: The voices belong to whoever owns them; `dialogue/speakers.json` covers six of eighteen actor names and that mismatch is the root cause rather than any one file's omission.

infos.x: Whatever the tide leaves and whatever the desk wants. That's most people here. If you're asking who decides which, it's the writ house, and they'll decide it about you too before the week is out.

Mine are set out on a schedule and the schedule is on the wall behind me. Yours are whatever is written on your writ, and if you have not read it, read it. People come back here angry about a line they signed under.

Born here, or near enough that the difference only matters to a clerk. My people worked the sap roads before the roads were the Empire's, and they work them still, and they're paid in a coin the Empire prints.
The Office trained me and the Office posted me, and where I was born is on a form in Gideon that no one has asked to see in nine years. Was there something you actually wanted?
Name it and I'll tell you if it's worth the walk. Ask me for the way and I'll give you that too, but ask the carters first, because they've been there this season and I haven't.

I know the places that appear in a ledger, which is not the same as knowing them. Soulrest, Gideon, Stormhold. If you want the road rather than the entry, ask a man who has walked it and take the second answer as well as the first.
There's always someone. Give me the name and I'll tell you if they're still here. And if they're not, I'll tell you which way they went. Who is it?
If they hold a writ, they exist and I can find them. If they do not, then as far as this desk is concerned there is no such person, and I would think carefully before telling me their name.
Nothing I sell. Food if you're hungry and a dry board if it rains, and I won't take coin for either, because taking coin for it makes it a trade and then the Office wants its share.
Stamps, copies, amendments and a witness if you need one witnessed. Everything on that list has a fee and the fee is the same for you as it is for the man behind you, whatever he tells you he paid.

Sap in the wet season, salvage in the dry, and the writ says one thing and the year says another. They don't check. They only check when there's a reason to check, and then they check everything at once.
I write down what walks through that door. It is not interesting and it is not supposed to be, and the day it becomes interesting is the day something has gone very wrong upriver.

Ask. That's it, that's the advice. No one in this province tells you a thing you haven't asked for, and the ones who do are selling you something. Walk into a town, ask what people are saying, and you'll know more than the road told you.

Carry your writ where you can reach it and do not let another hand hold it. The second thing: this desk answers what it is asked and nothing beyond it, and every desk in the province is the same desk. Ask badly and you will be told the truth and leave knowing less.
You want the town for that, not me. Ask in the square, ask twice, and believe the version you hear from two people who don't like each other.
This desk does not deal in what people are saying. It deals in what people have signed. If you want the other, the door is behind you and the square is past it.
Not to a stranger with a fresh stamp on his case, no. Come back when the stamp's gone soft and ask me again. How long are you here?

Everything I know is written down, and everything written down is copied, and the copy goes to Soulrest to be read against the Drowned Tally. So no. But I will tell you this much for free: it has not been read against anything since Second Seed.
